analysis_basis: Ghidra pseudocode and local SQLite call/string reference index for the supplied main executable; no runtime trace or game capture.

observed: Startup calls the layout resource preloader.
The preloader iterates a registered resource-name array and formats Layout/%s.Nin_NX_NVN.zs.
The opened resource is cached in an array indexed by the same loop index.
page_archive_preload.limitation: This preloader path does not explain the five Layout .szs archives in the RomFS inventory.

observed: 0x14c3cf0 initializes the layout manager and registers the LytAllocator resource allocator.
0x14c49e0 iterates a configured list of resource names and calls 0x14bfe60 for each.
0x14bebd0 formats Layout/%s.Nin_NX_NVN.zs, opens that archive, then requests a nested %s.arc member and registers an accessor for it.
layout_manager.limitation: The observed path proves a .zs archive route for this manager. It does not expose a condition selecting between same-name .zs and .szs candidates for each PRT1 reference.

observed: 0x14c77a0 looks up the named resource in the layout manager, obtains its accessor, and delegates loading through the layout resource interface.
0x191c8d0 formats %s.bflyt and requests it from the accessor using resource type value 0x626c7974.
0x1cf1230 creates an embedded layout object when the child entry is not yet materialized.
0x1ceb3e0 formats %s.bflyt from the requested child-layout name and initializes the resource accessor.
0x1cf2330 constructs an EuiAllocator:<locale><layout-name> resource key before constructing/loading the accessor.
0x1cf43a0 appends a suffix to the resource key and requests a BFLYT resource through the accessor.
embedded_prt1_layout.limitation: The pseudocode does not reveal an explicit .zs/.szs precedence branch at the PRT1 child lookup. The EuiAllocator key is visible, but the archive searched for each duplicate candidate is not resolved by this static call path.

part_ambiguities.reason: The loader chain proves name-based BFLYT resource requests and a .zs manager route, but does not prove which archive/accessor wins for the duplicate .zs/.szs BFLYT names.

native_updates.observed: Compares current date/time fields with cached values, obtains the localized STR_Week resource, and updates multiple text entries on MainScreen when relevant date/time fields change.
native_updates.limit: Some pane/resource identifiers are passed through opaque data and remain unnamed.

native_updates.observed: Writes four additional indexed text resources to MainScreen-bound controls.
native_updates.limit: The concrete pane names represented by the indexed resource keys are not decoded.

native_updates.observed: Iterates 11 STR_KeyIcon entries and refreshes their icon/control text on MainScreen when the source values differ.
native_updates.limit: The exact controller-style and key-to-icon mapping is not fully decoded from the opaque table.

native_updates.observed: Resolves the MainScreen child pane /L_Clock_00 and routes the clock update through its bound component helper.
native_updates.limit: The complete time formatting and visibility conditions are not established by this wrapper alone.

native_updates.observed: Checks the MainUiClockEnable setting, calls two MenuDevice update helpers, and updates MenuDevice clock-related text/state based on the current clock value.
native_updates.limit: This function is a MenuDevice component update; it does not prove the full MainScreenSmartPhone controller or screen-open lifecycle.

main_screen_and_hud.evidence_limit: No exact native reference to MainScreenSmartPhone was found in the current 62-name layout-reference sample. The absence of that exact string does not rule out dynamically named construction or a controller that targets another layout.

action_name_table.observed: Builds/caches the named action table; callers use its indexed names when dispatching UI control state changes.

observed: 0x14845a0 translates an action index into a named control action and dispatches it through the control action tree.
Dispatch updates per-action state flags and routes into animation/action objects through virtual calls.
The helper distinguishes action start/update paths and uses separate methods for the different action modes.
control_action_dispatch.limitation: The function chain does not map platform button/touch input to each action index, nor establish the complete focus restoration, modal stack, or screen lifecycle.

cursor_binding.observed: Looks up Cursor-related panes and uses P_BtnFocusKey, then C_Cursor, as cursor candidates; B_Hit is used as a fallback hit-related pane for the second cursor component.
cursor_binding.limitation: The wrapper proves resource binding/fallback names, not the complete geometry hit-test or focus-navigation algorithm.

observed: 0x1671db0 creates a BoundingCtrl helper for a UI-system record.
0x1670400 reads UISysBoundingUseCursor; when enabled, it resolves a cursor-related resource, creates the cursor binding, and configures four cursor channels.
0x1671c00 dispatches UISysBounding, UISysScrollBtnList, and UISysScrollSign records to separate virtual handlers.
bounding_control.limitation: This UISysBounding controller is not proof of the BND1 BoundingPane hit-test implementation; coordinate conversion, hit precedence, and platform input routing remain unresolved.

focus_callback.observed: Updates control-state flags, emits the corresponding indexed action, and notifies its registered callback/listener when its state guards permit.
focus_callback.limitation: The external caller and all guard meanings are not resolved.

observed: 0x11e6d70 selects CmnDialogSmartPhone when its mode field equals 1; otherwise it selects CmnDialog.
The constructor creates and attaches CommonDialogPage and CommonDialogBGPage objects.
0x11e8960 branches on a dialog state code and updates state-specific controls; 0x11e9210 refreshes STR_KeyIcon and KeyGuide entries for the selected dialog state.
0x11e96a0 iterates child/page slots 0 through 7 and applies state/animation operations to those slots.
common_dialog_controller.limitation: This traces a dialog component, not the global modal stack. Open/close/back sequencing, focus return, and teardown are still unproven.

observed: 0x1dd0c20 configures state transitions in a reusable selectable-widget controller; the state IDs correspond by order to the 18-name enum string initialized by 0x1dd37a0.
The transition table includes key selection/decision/cancel, inverse-direction selection, touch selection/decision/cancel, inverse-touch variants, and valid/invalid state changes.
0x1dd0b40 also initializes cursor-related behavior using the *Cursor tag and enables an auxiliary Draggable path when that userData value is present.
limits: Transition trigger strings and state IDs are statically mapped, but the physical button/touch event producer and callback order are not identified.
The helper calls 0x1caf820/0x1caf8d0/0x1caf990 add state-transition metadata; their opaque flag arguments are preserved raw and not assigned undocumented meanings.
The common widget family includes a slider/button caller but this does not establish that every UI control uses the same state machine.

control_profiles.common_pane_actions: B_Btn_00:Hit and B_Btn_00:Cursor are the dominant bindings; some layouts use B_Hit/N_Cursor_00 variants.
B_Hit:Hit and N_BtnFocusKey:Cursor (with B_Btn_00 variants in a small subset).
B_Hit:Hit and N_BtnFocusKey:Cursor (one record has an empty cursor pane name).

cnt1_asset_correlations.observed: The 18 action names present on every LpUniteButton CNT1 entry match the native selectable-state transition vocabulary; ButtonNormal/Check/Repeat CNT1 profiles likewise match the native named action table and their type-specific Check/Repeat emitters.
cnt1_asset_correlations.limit: This is a static format/native name correlation. It does not prove which runtime controller instance binds a given CNT1 record, the physical event source, or animation invocation timing.

user_button_animation_bindings.observed: The initializer resolves the four named animation/user-data tags and attaches them to the UserButton controller; missing entries use the UB_Unselect path as fallback.
limits: The tag bindings do not prove which input callback invokes each tag or what frames/timing are used.

shared_button_widget.observed: The shared button setup configures selection-loop/effect-invalid tags and equip-in/equip-out transitions, then delegates common cursor/focus setup to 0x1dd0b40.
limits: These tags prove available state/action names for this widget family; they do not identify the global event source or screen lifecycle.

known_action_emitters.limit: The external event source and full guard-bit meanings are unresolved.

known_action_emitters.limit: Does not identify which platform or game event caused the invalidation.

known_action_emitters.observed: For ButtonCheck (mode 2), emits Uncheck when its boolean argument is false; it updates the stored bit and notifies a callback first.
known_action_emitters.limit: Control mode and boolean producer are not named.

known_action_emitters.limit: The touch repeat producer/rate is not present in this method.

known_action_emitters.observed: For ButtonFocusActive (mode 4), emits Active or Inactive based on its boolean argument, with callback notification and stored-state updates.

focus_and_action_dispatch.known_action_emitters_summary: Static callsites now connect action IDs 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, and 12 to concrete control methods. ButtonCheck, ButtonRepeat, and ButtonFocusActive are independently identified by the native type resolver. The remaining action names are present in the lookup table but their full producers are not identified in this path. Touchscreen handling is now traced to named TouchSelect/TouchUnselect UI messages through the 61-entry native message registry; this remains distinct from the 13 control-animation action names, and recipient-to-state-machine binding is unresolved.

button_control_type_resolver.inheritance: The literal type Inherit is recursively resolved against the related parent/control record rather than mapped to one fixed mode.
button_control_type_resolver.observed: The resolver returns a valid marker and mode ID; the caller constructs mode-specific control state and callbacks.
limits: The type IDs identify controller families, but do not by themselves identify concrete physical input bindings.

data_dispatch.observed: Reads UI component type names (including LpUniteButton) from the parsed layout/UI data and selects a type-specific virtual handler. The LpUniteButton branch selects vtable offset +0x18; the handler receives the component context and parsed record.
data_dispatch.limit: The pseudocode proves the type-to-slot selection and call shape, not the indirect method body, event source, or callback timing.

followup_dispatch.observed: Selects a second type-specific virtual handler for the same UI component type family. In callers 0x112a6f0, 0x135c150, and 0x1461b90 this dispatch occurs after 0x1db2140 in the builder path.
followup_dispatch.limit: Indirect handler targets and per-type effects are unresolved; this is not proof of screen lifecycle or input routing.

controller_factory_correlations.observed: 0x112a910 stores the class token AppUniteBtnCtrl and creates a child control; its builder caller 0x112a6f0 also calls shared widget setup 0x130ca20, which delegates to 0x1dd0b40.
0x1db5cf0 stores the class token UniteBtnCtrl and constructs the controller; 0x1db3020 calls this factory and then the common 18-state initializer 0x1dd0b40.

ui_component_dispatch.relationship_limit: The matching LpUniteButton name in CNT1 and these native controller/type-dispatch paths provide a stronger family-level correlation. No recovered indirect handler body assigns all 91 CNT1 records to a specific factory, screen, or event source.

observed: The application initializer creates and initializes the touch-manager object.
The manager registers its update node through 0x1979ff0 and initializes per-pointer bookkeeping arrays.
The related application teardown at 0x1536d90 calls 0x14b8ce0; that path clears touch-manager storage through 0x14b8d20.
Reads up to 16 platform touch states.
Matches platform contact IDs to persistent UI pointer records, updates coordinates and contact flags, and handles new/unmatched contacts.
coordinate_path_observed: The 0x1302a70 path also calls GetTouchScreenStates<16>, filters contact points against a computed screen rectangle, and retains normalized coordinates.
0x1303a10 obtains a UI rectangle, returns the last accepted contact and normalized u/v coordinates; 0x1302f10 updates/interpolates pointer state.
limitations: 0x14b8f60 has no direct caller in the indexed call graph, consistent with indirect update dispatch but not proving the exact scheduler edge.
The coordinate helper path and pointer-manager path both sample HID touch, but no exact call edge between those separate paths is shown.

observed: The processor scans pointer records, hit-tests layout/control geometry recursively, records a target control, and calls the generic UI message emitter.
The message emitter validates IDs below 61, indexes the native message-name table, and forwards the resulting named message through 0x15329b0.
The native message registry maps 0x2d to TouchSelect and 0x2e to TouchUnselect.
hit_test_and_messages.overlap_with_control_state_machine: The 18-state widget machine contains a TouchSelect trigger (state 0 to 8). Its exit trigger spells TouchUnSelect with capital S, while the message registry spells TouchUnselect. This lexical overlap is evidence of a related touch vocabulary, not proof that this pointer message is delivered to a particular LpUniteButton state machine.
limitations: This establishes pointer-to-named-message routing within the UI system, but not the final recipient handler, FocusTouch/UnFocusTouch/DecideTouch action emission, or platform-button mapping.
Message code 0x22 is recorded as a name-table index only; this analysis does not infer what “Decide_Invalid” means in the hit-test branch.

The local direct-call index does not connect poller 0x14b8f60 to processor 0x14b94c0. Their shared manager/pointer data context supports grouping them as one subsystem, but an indirect runtime edge has not been traced.

npad_sampling.observed: The initializer calls nn::hid::InitializeNpad and nn::hid::InitializeTouchScreen before delegating to 0x14ced60.
npad_sampling.direct_callsite_status: No direct-call rows point to these GetNpadStates import thunks in the local call index. Their use through indirect/system paths is not ruled out.
npad_sampling.limitation: No physical Npad button to UI message/action mapping has been recovered.

layout_walk.observed: Recursively walks layout panes during layout setup and invokes effect-link, text-adjustment, and capture handlers.

observed: 0x14c89c0 constructs the registered pane type ScissorPane, and 0x14c8d00 sets an enable byte and copies four 32-bit rectangle values.
The viewport_geometry_path shows where the values are computed and written; GPU render consumption remains unresolved.
scissor_pane.limitation: The native path proves geometry and object update, but not the final NVN scissor command, clipping coordinate space, or nested-clip intersection rule.

observed: The viewport/layout adjustment path 0x148ff20 reaches 0x1496460 after computing a clipped content/visible extent.
0x1496460 lazily creates and stores a ScissorPane object when one is not already present, then invokes 0x14c8d00 with the computed four-value rectangle.
0x1496530 derives the four rectangle values from the resolved layout/ancestor properties and the caller-supplied viewport dimensions; 0x1496460 also returns the resulting width/height to the parent.
The cleanup path 0x1495d80 destroys the associated object through 0x14c8b70.
viewport_geometry_path.limit: This proves rectangle calculation, ScissorPane object creation/update, and cleanup in the viewport-adjustment path. It does not expose the final NVN scissor command, clipping coordinate space, or nested-clip intersection rule.

ui2dsys_type_dispatch.observed: Dispatches parsed ui2dsys type names to distinct virtual handlers; 0x1671c00 handles the three UISys* types in the same family.
ui2dsys_type_dispatch.limitation: Slot selection and builder order are static evidence; vtable targets, per-type runtime effects, asset-instance binding, and input/event behavior remain unresolved.

nested_factory_paths.evidence: The nested dispatcher compares the type name and calls +0x90. Candidate pointer sequences contain 0x1671d70 at that slot; 0x1671d70 calls 0x1671db0, which calls the confirmed BoundingCtrl factory.

The nested dispatcher compares the type name and calls +0x98. Candidate sequences contain 0x1672110 at that slot; nearby follow-up implementation 0x1672150 calls the confirmed ScrollBtnListCtrl factory. The short slot-target body is not decompiled.

The nested dispatcher compares the type name and calls +0xa0. Candidate sequences contain 0x16724b0 at that slot; nearby follow-up implementation 0x16724f0 calls the confirmed ScrollSignCtrl factory. The short slot-target body is not decompiled.

fleu_relation.unresolved: The 15 FLEU records are structurally bound to USD1 keys; native renderer consumes several other matching keys. The native update function applying FLEU arrays and their timing are not proven. C_Id now has a static asset profile, but no exact native string consumer or runtime semantics are established.

c_id_static_profile.observed: All 11 C_Id FLEU records bind uniquely to a same-archive USD1 int32 value of 0. They occur on color-named tracks in common control/footer assets; the three arrays have lengths 3 or 5 according to the record base_count.
c_id_static_profile.limit: These patterns constrain the data context but do not identify the native custom-property consumer or array element meanings.

remaining_evidence_needed: A direct runtime/resource-manager trace or complete allocator lookup logic showing which archive supplies each duplicate PRT1 name, including .szs cases.
Caller/vptr identification for MainScreenSmartPhone open/update/close and its relationship to MainScreen HUD state.
Associate candidate pointer arrays 0x315b0d0 and 0x30fc6b8 with live component objects, then decompile/resolve remaining handlers for all component types and bind records to screens.

Resolve Npad button producers, named UI message delivery for all 13 control actions, recipient/CNT1 callback order, modal push/pop, focus restoration, and screen lifecycle. TouchSelect/TouchUnselect names are known, but their recipient state machine is not.
A native FLEU application path mapping arrays to named userData values and animation frame timing.
